description: Wings exact to the last scale, a lantern-sized dragon guessed at, and a jet of flame three times its length.
lore: No dragon was ever anywhere to be remembered. What there was, in a hundred countries at once, was the telling of one, and a telling said often enough, to enough people listening, weighs as much here as a life does. So this is not the memory of an animal; it is the memory of an account, and you can see the difference at ten paces. Whoever did most of the remembering had never seen a dragon — no one has — but they had lain in a summer meadow once, watching the irises being worked over close up, and when the account ran out, that is what came to hand. The wings are the best-made thing on it: four of them, violet banded with pink, exact to the last scale. The body is a grey-green guess the size of a lantern. What got looked at came out sharp. What got taken on trust came out approximate.

Then it opens its mouth and puts out flame three times its own length, and the joke stops there. The fire is the one detail every retelling in every country kept, so it came through whole and unworn, entirely indifferent to the size of the thing carrying it. [[characters/54bead23|Osric]], new enough to still count in living years, called it a moth with opinions, at a range he has since revised. The tellers do his eyebrows when they tell it, and he sits and lets them, which is most of why the fire likes him. Being wrong about a creature does not make it harmless. It only decides which parts of it are.

[[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] keeps a page of dragon accounts in [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]] and cannot get two of the woken to agree on wings, size, colour, or where the hoard was kept. The page carries one sentence every hand has signed. The fire is right.
